result.title: Preface
result.summary: The Public Safety Personnel Retirement System (PSPRS), Corrections Officer Retirement Plan, and Elected Officials’ Retirement Plan list their trustees and administrators, including Chairman Scott McCarty and Administrator Michael F. Townsend. The document provides PSPRS’s Phoenix address, telephone and fax numbers, website, and staff roles. Acting as administrators of the PSPRS Trust, the Board of Trustees issues a request for proposal for non-discretionary investment consultant services. Submissions are due by 5:00 p.m. MST on October 29, 2021. PSPRS contact Laura Long is listed with her telephone number and email address.

result.title: REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL NON-DISCRETIONARY INVESTMENT CONSULTANT SERVICES
result.summary: The RFP seeks a non-discretionary investment consultant to support PSPRS’s CIO and investment team in implementing policy across a roughly $17 billion, diversified three-plan public pension trust; its separate fiduciary consultant, NEPC, is excluded. Services include alternative-asset planning, market research, sourcing and vetting investments, investment and operational due diligence, data verification, performance and risk reporting, record reconciliation, meeting support, CIO projects, institutional-practice advice, and activity reports. Minimum qualifications require capacity, relevant experience with public pension trusts of at least $10 billion, and verifiable activity and resources. Evaluation weights are capabilities (30%), experience and staffing (25%), service delivery and operational plan (25%), and cost (20%); written proposals and possible interviews are considered. Proposals require a signed letter and information on the firm, approach, experience and staff, references, and fees, plus disclosures and supporting details. The RFP sets submission, questions, revision, exceptions, contract-term, award, and extensive legal and operational conditions. The System may reject all proposals and need not select the lowest-cost respondent.

nodes.title: BACKGROUND INFORMATION
nodes.summary: The Public Safety Personnel Retirement System Board issued an RFP to hire a non-discretionary investment consultant for the CIO and Investment Team. Services include cross-asset-class expertise, research and assistance identifying and vetting opportunities, and advisory portfolio-allocation guidance. Established in 1968, the System administers three defined-benefit plans—PSPRS, CORP, and EORP—with lifelong pension benefits. As of June 30, 2020, 239 employers and 59,387 members participated; assets totaled about $17 billion on September 10, 2021. Policy allocations are 67% Capital Appreciation (private/public equity, real estate, real assets), 22% Contractual Income (private credit, core bonds), and 10% Diversifying Strategies (hedge funds, risk parity). The Trust holds 232 drawdown funds and 15 hedge funds. The Board delegated investment decision-making authority to the System Administrator and has used non-discretionary consultants since 2008 to support a diversified portfolio, including alternatives. This procurement updates those services. The Board’s separate fiduciary consultant, NEPC, is not part of the bid.

nodes.title: SCOPE OF SERVICES
nodes.summary: The Trust seeks a non-discretionary investment consultant to support its investment team and implementation of the Board’s Investment Policy Statement. Services include annual alternative-asset strategy and implementation planning; access to updated proprietary market research, emerging-issue reports, due-diligence findings and manager deal-history databases; sourcing suitable funds, co-investments and direct investments; and written investment and operational due diligence, with updates when material changes occur. Operational reviews cover governance, legal/regulatory matters, service providers, policies, reporting, controls and operations; investment reviews cover strategy, performance history, process, team and committees. The consultant will verify manager data and provide monthly/quarterly performance, holdings, commitments, concentration, risk, valuation and market reporting. It will also reconcile investment and custodian records when requested; prepare for and attend meetings, lead asset-class calls, and support investment discussions, working with NEPC. Additional duties include CIO-assigned projects and institutional-practice advice, plus monthly online activity reports covering recommendations, due diligence and project status.

nodes.title: MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS
nodes.summary:
MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS
All proposals received on or before the proposal due date at the location specified in this solicitation will be evaluated to determine whether they meet the following minimum qualifications:
1. Proposers must have the capacity to provide all service requirements identified in this solicitation;
2. Proposers must have experience with providing all service requirements identified in this solicitation to public pension trusts with assets under management of at least $10 billion; and 3. Proposers must have a verifiable history of activity and adequate resources to carry out the service requirements in this solicitation.

nodes.title: EVALUATION CRITERIA
nodes.summary: Proposals will be evaluated using written submissions and/or finalist interviews, though interviews are not guaranteed, so written proposals should include all information firms want considered. Criteria are: relevant experience and current staffing capacity (25%); capabilities in strategic advice, identifying and evaluating investments, operational and investment due diligence, manager performance reporting and monitoring, and back-office support (30%); ability to meet service requirements, communicate with the CIO and investment team, Trustees, and Board consultant, address ongoing and special issues and concerns, and provide a sound operational plan and qualified assigned staff (25%); and overall proposed cost (20%).

nodes.title: FORMAT AND CONTENT OF THE PROPOSAL
nodes.summary:
FORMAT AND CONTENT OF THE PROPOSAL
Proposals must include the information below, presented in a clear, comprehensive, and concise manner to illustrate the proposing firm’s capabilities.

nodes.title: INSTRUCTIONS
nodes.summary: The RFP specifies a signed transmittal letter and a five-part proposal: firm background, scope understanding, experience/staff, references, and costs. Applicants must disclose organizational history and changes, services, insurance, legal/regulatory and debarment matters, qualifications, finances, conflicts, registrations, methodology, comparable work, staff details and continuity plans, availability, five references, terminated pension clients, and fees/expenses. The System may verify submissions. The anticipated term is three years plus two one-year extensions. Proposals are due electronically October 29, 2021; withdrawal or revision is permitted before the deadline. Questions are due October 8, through the designated contact; other staff contact is prohibited. Exceptions require a separate, justified statement and may render a proposal nonresponsive. Award is based on best value; discussions and interviews may occur. Contract terms cover representations, anti-collusion, document precedence, amendments, public records/audits, proposal validity, protests, subcontracting, licensing, independent-contractor status, indemnity, insurance, termination, ownership, notices, confidentiality, legal remedies, Arizona law, nondiscrimination, immigration, fiduciary duties, nonexclusivity, force majeure, emergency continuity, transition, data security, offsets, performance, debarment, claims, accuracy, and funding availability.

nodes.title: DISCLAIMER
nodes.summary:
DISCLAIMER
The System is not under any obligation to accept the lowest bid or lowest fee or, indeed, choose any of the respondents to this RFP for an engagement; and the System may employ any criteria it deems appropriate, whether or not referenced in this RFP, in evaluating the proposals submitted.
